headline: Granted administrative approval of revised Parmenter Road repaving plans, citing reduced wetland impact.
summary: A wetland permit request for 523 Mammoth Road, which would disturb 2,300 square feet of wetland, was discussed. Changes to the conservation overlay zoning ordinance were also raised. The group agreed to ask applicants to make plans available two weeks before they meet, and to note conservation issues on extra-large plans.
decisions: Agreed to ask that plans be available two weeks before applicants meet, and that extra-large plans include a summary note on conservation issues.
Granted administrative approval of the revised Parmenter Road repaving plans, unanimously.
Approved the minutes of the October 13, 2026 meeting as presented, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: The Commission agreed to request that plans be made available two weeks before an applicant meets with them and that for extra-large plans, the applicant include a summary note referring to the conservation issues.

D. Lievens moved to grant administrative approval of the revised plans, based on the assertion that they are using the 2002 plans with reduction in wetland impact. B. Maxwell seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.
D. Lievens moved to accept the minutes of the October 13, 2026, meeting as presented. B. Maxwell seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.

decision_titles: Two-week plan availability and notes for applicants
Revised repaving plan for Parmenter Road
plain_text:
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, October 27, 2026
Draft Minutes
1 Present: Marge Badois, Chair; Gene Harrington, Vice Chair; Deb Lievens, member; Bob Maxwell, 
2 member; David Heafey, member; Elkel Bickford, member; Gary Della Grotta, alternate member; Susan 
3 Malouin, alternate member
4
5 Absent: Michael Speltz, alternate member
6
7 Others Present: Michael Bazegian, GIS Manager/Comprehensive Planner
8
9
10 Call to Order and Roll Call
11 M. Badois called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m.
12
13 DRC/Dredge & Fill - 523 Mammoth Road -- LLC Site Plan - Map 15 Lot 2
14 George Chadwick of Bedford Design Consultants and Luke Hurley, certified wetlands scientist, appeared 
15 before the Commission to discuss a wetland permit for 2,300 square feet of wetland disturbance. G. 
16 Chadwick explained their intent to reroute an existing wetland area/drainage ditch that bisects the 
17 property around the property via a 24-inch reinforced concrete pipe back into the wetland into which it 
18 currently drains.
19
20 G. Chadwick described the property, which consists of three merged parcels. There is a 10,570 square 
21 foot ponded area that does not have a wetland buffer; however, the larger wetland on the property 
22 does have a buffer. There will be 11,529 square foot of wetland buffer impact for which they intend to 
23 submit a CUP. The building will store electrical supplies.
24
25 L. Hurley said there is no wildlife in the disturbed wetland; it is a drainage ditch. No hydrology is being 
26 shut off, as the runoff is being redirected. The wildlife conservation measures required by the NHF&G 
27 are on the plan, consisting of contractor notification about turtles and cottontails.
28
29 M. Badois asked if the wetland was part of the Little Cohas and was told it was not. G. Chadwick pointed 
30 out adjoining land with a conservation easement. 
31
32 M. Badois asked if NHDES granting the wetland permit would change the buffers. G. Chadwick said it 
33 would alter the buffer as it stands today; however, the alteration has already been calculated into the 
34 11,529 square foot impact. 
35
36 M. Badois noted the application was submitted on September 18th. She did not know about it until the 
37 applicant emailed her on October 22nd, asking about it. The Commission was not notified by the Town 
38 Clerk, which is the established procedure that is not being followed.
39
40 Commission Comments: The Commission had no concerns. 
41
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, October 27, 2026
Draft Minutes
42 Public Comment
43 There were no members of the public present.
44
45 Old Business
46
47 Musquash/Hickory Hill
48 M. Badois asked that the kiosk be moved to the top of the parking lot. The big sign was moved instead. 
49 DPW will look into building a new sign in this location, as the existing sign is rotting.
50
51 CPI Solar Array
52 M. Badois noted the Commission received information on the array the day it was presented at the 
53 Commission meeting; they had no opportunity to review the information. Sylvia von Aulock, in her role 
54 as interim Town Planner, sent a memo to NHDES asking that they investigate the wetland that was 
55 obliterated. M. Badois noted the wetland that was cleared to the edge of is the Musquash swamp, which
56 should have a 100-foot buffer. Restoration and mitigation will be needed.
57
58 Maps
59 New maps have been printed and are available.
60
61 New Business
62
63 Conservation Overlay District
64 M. Badois said the conservation overlay district does not clearly describe what is allowed in the buffer. 
65 For example, logging has been interpreted as clear-cutting. She asked if it was possible to edit the 
66 conservation overlay zoning ordinance. The Commission discussed the repercussions of the zoning 
67 ordinance being opened for modification. They questioned whether timber tax was collected as a result 
68 of the clear-cutting. 
69
70 Availability of Plans and Notice
71 M. Badois noted applicants used to provide a week's notice before appearing before the Commission. 
72 The Commission asked that two weeks' notice be given, to allow them time to review the associated 
73 materials. If an applicant needs to return, they could automatically be placed on the next Agenda. The 
74 Commission could make exceptions as needed. They also discussed requiring applicants to highlight 
75 where they think they are close to conservation issues on extra-large plans.
76
77 The Commission agreed to request that plans be made available two weeks before an applicant meets 
78 with them and that for extra-large plans, the applicant include a summary note referring to the 
79 conservation issues. 
80
81 Monitoring
82 M. Badois said Plummer needs to be monitored after the end of hunting season. She will look at dates.
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, October 27, 2026
Draft Minutes
83
84 G. Harrington offered to monitor the property behind the Grange.
85
86 D. Heafey asked about utilizing OpenGov to track the monitoring of properties. M. Badois said OpenGov 
87 is gradually being put into place. With the departure of the former Town Manager, this process might 
88 take longer than anticipated. She noted the quality of the Town's GIS system and recommended the 
89 Commission members use it instead of the online version. 
90
91 NHACC Annual Meeting
92 M. Badois said the NHACC Annual Meeting is on November 7, 2026.
93
94 Parmenter Road
95 The Commission reviewed the revised repaving plan for Parmenter Road.
96
97 D. Lievens moved to grant administrative approval of the revised plans, based on the assertion that 
98 they are using the 2002 plans with reduction in wetland impact. B. Maxwell seconded the motion. The 
99 motion carried unanimously. 
100
101 Approval of Minutes
102
103 D. Lievens moved to accept the minutes of the October 13, 2026, meeting as presented. B. Maxwell 
104 seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.
105
106 Adjournment
107
108 G. Harrington made a motion to adjourn. D. Heafey seconded the motion. The motion carried 
109 unanimously. 
110
111 The meeting was adjourned at 8:15 p.m.
112
113 Respectfully submitted, 
114
115 Beth Hanggeli
116 Recording Secretary
